verdict.reason: The claimed validation gap is real. assertValidBlock's table branch validates only Array.isArray(cell.blocks) (controller.ts:292-298) and never cell.style, while serializeCellStyle dereferences it unguarded (docs-tree.ts:197-198, `const s = cell.style; if (s.backgroundColor)`), reached via buildCellNode/buildRowNode from the table branch of buildBlockNode (docs-tree.ts:275,298,307). Likewise the non-table branch checks only Array.isArray(b.inlines) (controller.ts:309-311) while buildInlineNode reads inline.text.length and serializeInlineStyle(inline.style) (docs-tree.ts:251,254), and serializeInlineStyle immediately reads style.bold (docs-tree.ts:72). So `{blocks:[{id:'t',type:'table',style:{},tableData:{columnWidths:[1],rows:[{cells:[{blocks:[]}]}]}}]}` or `inlines:[null]` throws a TypeError inside the doc.update callback (controller.ts:163-165) -> HTTP 500 instead of the 400 the guard's header comment (controller.ts:126-135) says it exists to produce. I searched for a counterexample and found none: api-v1.module.ts:20-45 registers no pipe/interceptor for this controller; the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-72) is inert because the handler body is typed `unknown` (metatype Object, skipped by Nest's toValidate) with no DTO; writeDocsRoot (docs-tree.ts:541-589) performs no normalization and the only @wafflebase/docs imports are DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE / DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE / normalizeBlockStyle (docs-tree.ts:28-32); no ExceptionFilter exists in packages/backend/src to remap the TypeError; and the controller spec (docs-content.controller.spec.ts:408-506) has no cell.style or inline-item rejection test. Impact is bounded (buildTreeChildren runs before any tree mutation at docs-tree.ts:546, so no data corruption), but it is a genuine unguarded-dereference crash on a reachable API path, in the correctness lane.

mergedFrom.summary: DOCX_ALIGNMENTS lookup walks Object.prototype, so `constructor`/`toString`/`__proto__` bypass the "closed map" and land in <w:jc w:val>
`DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` lookup walks the prototype chain, so `alignment` values like `toString`/`constructor`/`valueOf` bypass the `?? 'left'` fallback

finding.summary: `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` lookup is not actually closed — prototype keys (`toString`, `constructor`, `__proto__`, `valueOf`) resolve to inherited values that get interpolated into `w:jc/@w:val`
finding.evidence: `const align = DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string] ?? 'left'` indexes a plain object literal, so the prototype chain is consulted. `style.alignment === 'toString'` yields `Object.prototype.toString` (a function), which is `!== 'left'` and is stringified into `<w:jc w:val="function toString() { [native code] }"/>`; `'__proto__'` yields `[object Object]`. The doc comment above claims `w:jc w:val` "can only ever carry an ST_Jc token", which is false — the result is a schema-invalid `ST_Jc` value that Word can refuse to open, i.e. the exact failure the change set out to prevent. Use `Object.hasOwn(DOCX_ALIGNMENTS, ...)`, a `Map`/`Set`, or `Object.create(null)`. The same pattern exists in the slides sink the comment cites as the model (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79`, `ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`), so it is not clamped there either.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence does not exist in the repository. `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS` is declared as `new Map<string, string>([...])` at packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:118 and read via `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS.get(style.alignment as string) ?? 'left'` at line 144 — not the object-literal bracket index `DOCX_ALIGNMENTS[style.alignment as string]` the finding quotes. `Map.prototype.get` consults only own entries, so `toString`/`constructor`/`valueOf`/`__proto__`/`hasOwnProperty` all return `undefined`, fall through to `'left'`, and are then suppressed by the `if (align !== 'left')` guard at line 145, emitting no `<w:jc>` element at all. The doc comment at lines 110-117 states this Map-over-object choice for precisely this reason, and packages/docs/test/export/docx-style-map.test.ts:161-176 asserts the exact prototype keys named in the finding produce no `<w:jc`. The secondary claim is equally wrong: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:79 is a JSDoc comment line about `lvl` clamping, not `ALGN[block.style.alignment] ?? 'l'`; `ALGN` is a Map at line 69 read via `ALGN.get(...)` at line 99, and grep for `ALGN` across packages/slides/src returns only lines 69, 99 and 249 — no bracket indexing anywhere. The prototype-chain vector requires bracket indexing of a plain object, which neither sink performs.

finding.summary: New block-style value validation covers only `alignment`; the numeric BlockStyle fields still accept arbitrary values that become NaN in layout
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` validates `style.alignment` only. `writeDocsRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:145) writes `marginTop: String(style.marginTop)` verbatim, and the read path does `partial.marginTop = Number(attrs.marginTop)` (docs-tree.ts:160) with `normalizeBlockStyle` being a bare spread (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:272-274, no numeric coercion/guard). A PUT with `style: { marginTop: "abc" }` therefore lands NaN in the model, and `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:383` does `y += block.style.marginTop`, NaN-ing the cumulative y for every subsequent block — the whole document renders blank/garbled for every collaborator, with no way to fix it from the UI. Same exposure for `marginBottom`, `lineHeight`, `textIndent`, `marginLeft`.

verdict.reason:
The claimed-missing numeric sanitization exists — twice — on the only PUT write path, and the reviewer's quoted evidence does not match this repository.

1) Write side. `writeDocsRoot` does NOT write `marginTop: String(style.marginTop)` verbatim. Every block (top-level, header/footer, and table-cell blocks) goes through `buildBlockNode` → `serializeBlockStyle` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:158-170), which explicitly filters the five numeric fields listed in `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS = ['lineHeight','marginTop','marginBottom','textIndent','marginLeft']` (docs-tree.ts:139-145):
   `const value = Number(style?.[field]); if (style?.[field] !== undefined && Number.isFinite(value)) attrs[field] = String(value);`
   A payload of `style: { marginTop: "abc" }` yields `Number("abc") === NaN`, fails `Number.isFinite`, and the attribute is simply omitted from the Yorkie tree — nothing non-finite is ever persisted. (docs-tree.ts:145 is the closing bracket of that constant array, not a `String(style.marginTop)` write; the reviewer's cited line does not exist.)

2) Read side. `parseBlockStyle` (docs-tree.ts:172-189) applies the same guard defensively for hand-edited/legacy CRDTs: `if (!(field in attrs)) continue; const value = Number(attrs[field]); if (Number.isFinite(value)) partial[field] = value;`. Omitted or non-finite fields fall back to `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE` via `normalizeBlockStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:216-223, 272-274). So the read path is `partial[field] = value` only when finite — not the unconditional `Number(attrs.marginTop)` the finding quotes.

3) Reachability. `writeDocsRoot` has exactly one production call site, packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:164; all other matches are specs. There is no alternate backend path that constructs block attributes bypassing `serializeBlockStyle`.

Additionally, there is no function named `assertValidBlockStyle` in docs-content.controller.ts at all; `assertValidBlock` (lines 254-312) deliberately validates shape only and its comment (lines 265-270) documents that style values are normalized downstream by `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` — which is exactly what the code does. NaN therefore cannot reach `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts` through this API, so the claimed blank/garbled-document data-loss scenario does not occur.

finding.summary: Block-style validation checks alignment values but still lets `style: {}` through, persisting the literal string "undefined" and NaN geometry into the CRDT
finding.evidence: The new test explicitly asserts `{ blocks: [{ id, type:'paragraph', style: {}, inlines: [] }] }` passes validation. `writeDocsRoot`'s `serializeBlockStyle` then produces `alignment: undefined` and `lineHeight: String(undefined) === 'undefined'` (docs-tree.ts:143-148); `parseBlockStyle` (line 159) does `Number('undefined') → NaN` and `normalizeBlockStyle` spreads that NaN over the default, so `marginTop`/`lineHeight` become NaN and `computeLayout`'s `y += block.style.marginTop` NaNs out the whole document layout. If the controller is now validating block-style *values*, the required numeric fields are the ones that actually corrupt the document when missing.

verdict.reason: The claimed missing guard exists. serializeBlockStyle (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:158-170) emits alignment only when it is a string (line 162) and each numeric field only when it is defined AND Number.isFinite (lines 163-168), so `style: {}` serializes to an empty attribute record — it never persists `alignment: undefined` or the literal string "undefined". parseBlockStyle (lines 172-189) mirrors this: it skips fields absent from attrs (line 184), assigns only finite numbers (line 186), and fills the remainder from DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE via normalizeBlockStyle (line 188; defaults at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:216-223 are all finite). Both write paths (buildBlockNode at docs-tree.ts:265 and :282) use the guarded serializer, and all read paths (:369, :409, :430) use the guarded parser, so no NaN can reach computeLayout from this route. A dedicated regression test at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.spec.ts:98-124 round-trips `style: {}` through writeDocsRoot/readDocsRoot and asserts alignment === 'left', every numeric value is finite, and the serialized style contains no 'undefined'. The reviewer's cited evidence line range (143-148) is the BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS array literal, not serializer logic.

finding.summary: PDF export sink was not routed through the new shared normalizer, so pasted `rgb(...)` and `#RGB` colors render as solid black
finding.evidence: `toRgbHexColor`'s doc comment claims "Every export sink that writes a color into an OOXML attribute needs this", and DOCX/PPTX were converted, but `styleColor()` still does `/^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/i` and returns `{r:0,g:0,b:0}` on any mismatch. The very inputs the diff says are routine (`rgb(255, 0, 0)` from `view/clipboard.ts` HTML paste, and `#abc` shorthand) therefore export as BLACK text in PDF, and via pdf-painter.ts:758 / pdf-table-painter.ts:173 as a black highlight/cell fill behind the text — visibly wrong output rather than a dropped attribute.

verdict.reason: The finding claims styleColor() in pdf-style-map.ts still uses a raw /^#?([0-9a-f]{6})$/i regex and was never routed through the shared toRgbHexColor normalizer. That is false in this working tree: pdf-style-map.ts:3 imports { defaultColorResolver, toRgbHexColor } from '../model/color.js', and styleColor at pdf-style-map.ts:151-152 does `const normalized = toRgbHexColor(defaultColorResolver(hex));`, returning black only when the normalizer yields undefined (no color at all). The quoted 6-hex-digit regex exists nowhere in source — a repo-wide grep finds it only in an archived design doc (docs/tasks/archive/2026/04/20260430-pdf-export-todo.md:724) and in unrelated slides canvas renderers. toRgbHexColor (model/color.ts:113-140) explicitly handles the two inputs the finding says would render black: #RGB shorthand (line 122-124) and rgb()/rgba() (line 134-139). Tests pin this: pdf-style-map.test.ts:104 asserts styleColor('rgb(255, 128, 0)') === {r:1,g:128/255,b:0} and :107 asserts styleColor('#f80') === {r:1,g:136/255,b:0}. The named downstream sinks (pdf-painter.ts:759, pdf-table-painter.ts:178) call this same normalized styleColor, so the alleged black highlight/cell-fill path does not exist.

finding.summary: Cell-style attribute removal uses a *range* over the whole cell subtree, so `backgroundColor` is also stripped from every inline (text highlight) and nested-table node inside the cell
finding.evidence: `applyCellStyle` now does `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, removeAttrs)` with `endPath = [...cellPath]` and last index +1 — a position range that spans the cell node AND all of its descendants (blocks, inlines, nested tables). Yorkie's tree style/removeStyle applies to every non-text node in the range (the same reason `setBlockType`'s `removeStyleByPath(blockPath, blockPath+1, ['listKind','listLevel'])` at line 1439 reaches inline nodes too — harmlessly, because those keys don't exist there). Here the attribute name collides: inline nodes store text highlight under the very same key `backgroundColor` (`serializeInlineStyle` line 122, `parseInlineStyle` line 177), and nested table cells store `backgroundColor`/`border*`/`padding`. So the new "No fill" reset (docs-table-context-menu.tsx:233 → `{ backgroundColor: undefined }`) silently deletes the highlight colour of every run in the cell and the fills/borders of any nested table — irreversible data loss in the CRDT. The in-memory cache is only patched for the cell (`cell.style = merged`), so the loss is invisible until reload/remote sync, and the added test (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2031) uses a cell whose inlines have no `backgroundColor`, so it cannot catch this. A per-node removal (or an explicit `removeStyleByPath` restricted to the cell element only, e.g. by re-setting the descendants' attrs) is needed.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence does not exist in the repository. `applyCellStyle` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2445-2480) does NOT call `tree.removeStyleByPath(cellPath, endPath, removeAttrs)`; at line 2472 it calls `removeCellNodeStyle(tree, cellPath, removeAttrs)`. That helper (lines 277-285) does `const from = tree.pathToIndex(cellPath); tree.removeStyle(from, from + 1, attrsToRemove);` — an index range covering only the cell's opening tag, so descendant inlines/nested-table cells (which start at from+1, a zero-width boundary overlap the range walk excludes) are untouched. The doc comment at 263-276 spells out exactly the hazard the finding describes and states this is the deliberate node-scoped workaround. A repo-wide grep confirms the only `removeStyle*` calls are removeCellNodeStyle (284) and the two block-level `removeStyleByPath` range calls at 1463 (headingLevel/listKind/listLevel) and 1920 — neither touches cell `backgroundColor`. `applyCellSpan` (2522) uses the same node-scoped helper for colSpan/rowSpan. Therefore no `backgroundColor` stripping of inlines or nested tables can occur via this path.
